style: Read this aloud clearly and naturally, at a moderate pace, for middle-school students learning English
lines: It's raining cats and dogs.
It means: It is raining very hard.
Bring an umbrella. It's raining cats and dogs out there!
A piece of cake.
It means: Something very easy.
The spelling test was a piece of cake. I knew every word.
Break the ice.
It means: Do or say something that helps people relax and start talking.
On the first day, our teacher played a name game to break the ice.
Under the weather.
It means: Feeling a little sick.
Maya stayed home today because she was feeling under the weather.
Spill the beans.
It means: Tell a secret, often too early.
Don't spill the beans about Dad's surprise party!
Hit the books.
It means: Study hard.
I have a big test tomorrow, so tonight I need to hit the books.
Once in a blue moon.
It means: Very rarely; almost never.
It snows in our town only once in a blue moon.
When pigs fly.
It means: Never. It will not happen.
"Will your little brother ever clean his room?" "Sure, when pigs fly!"
Hold your horses.
It means: Wait. Slow down and be patient.
Hold your horses! We can't open the presents until everyone is here.
Butterflies in my stomach.
It means: A nervous, fluttery feeling.
I had butterflies in my stomach before my piano recital.
In hot water.
It means: In trouble.
Jamal was in hot water after he forgot his homework three days in a row.
The ball is in your court.
It means: It is your turn to decide or to act.
I said sorry and asked to be friends again. Now the ball is in your court.
